- **Expectation:** effort/m per the existing label; "done" is the design doc plus a linked implementation breakdown, gated on the #6280 research entry condition.
- **Links:** core topic #6280; principles source #1240

**Notes:** This is the v1 (first-iteration) member of a four-part outline series (#6300–#6303) under core topic #6280. The later outlines (v2–v4) are deliberately thinner; this v1 carries the spike plan, so it is the one enriched in this pass. **Suggested approach:** Verify the entry condition on #6280, then draft the design doc against the four principles, then file the breakdown as native sub-issues per protocol §11.

## Spike step 5/5 landed — spike complete (#7917, PR #13236)

The bounded program interaction and the end-to-end spike run landed in [PR #13236](https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/13236) (merged `597aae2f64da`), closing #7917. The spike's five steps are now all landed: shell + agent-profile contract (#7913), MCP bridge translator (#7914), live end-to-end run (#7915), policy point (#7916, reconciled by #13202), and this step.

**What the run does** (`pkgs/id/tests/mcp_spike_e2e.rs`): an agent joins a local tic-tac-toe world over iroh, driven entirely through the host-side policy point — join, screen reads, subscribe, chat with a second participant, one ceiling-refused invoke of an unlisted program, one admitted invoke of the named program on the named object (arguments from the call, decided against the current screen revision), the result read back as a semantic diff, leave.

**Acceptance evidence** (laptop route, `nix develop` in `pkgs/id`, at the merged head):

1. *Scripted spike run completes end-to-end on a local world (P2P path)* — `cargo test --test mcp_spike_e2e`: passed, including 4 consecutive runs during development.
2. *Audit log complete, chain verifies* — the run's audit log holds exactly one event per action in script order (join, reads, subscribe, chat, the refused invoke, the admitted invoke, leave); the admitted invoke's event names the program and charges 1 program invocation; the refusal charges nothing; `verify_audit` passes over the signed chain; owner summary: 9 actions / 8 executed / 1 refusal, spend frames 4 · tool calls 7 · program invocations 1. The host journal, exported through the fixture recorder, independently holds both chats (sequences 2, 3) and the invocation's input (sequence 4).
3. *Conformance suite (shell + agent profile) passes* — `cargo test -p id-worlds shell_contract`: **20 passed, 0 failed**. Neighboring suites at the same head: `cargo test -p id-caps --lib` 253/253, `mcp_bridge_surface` 3/3, `mcp_bridge_e2e` 1/1, fmt clean.

**One protocol finding from the run**, recorded in the test: a commit's frames are generated together but their wire order is not contractual — a re-rendered view can land behind the semantic diff. A driver that takes the `screen_revision` token from a partially drained stream can lag the host's current revision by exactly that trailing view, and the host's stale-decision gate then refuses the invoke (observed live: `stale decision: input was decided against screen revision 0, current is 1`). The spike driver drains its own actions to quiescence before taking the token; the helper documents why. Worth carrying into any real MCP host driver for this contract.

2. **Design document exists** — `doc/2026-11-09_design_id6300_agents_in_worlds_v1.md`, present on current main (20,340 bytes, delivered by PR #7911, merged 2026-11-10). It covers one agent joining a world as an MCP-bridge client, reading screens, posting chat, and one bounded program interaction under a capability ceiling with a full audit log, plus agent identity, roles, and guardrails, per the #1240 Phase 14 principles.
3. **Implementation breakdown filed and linked** — native sub-issues #7913, #7914, #7915, #7916, #7917 (re-read via the sub-issues API this pass): **all five closed**. Carried forward on the record (not a remainder of this issue): the protocol finding in that same note — a commit's frames are generated together but wire order is not contractual, so a real MCP host driver for this contract must drain to quiescence before taking a `screen_revision` token. It is documented in `pkgs/id/tests/mcp_spike_e2e.rs` and in the note above, where any follow-on driver work under #6280 will find it.
